pages.title: The Art of Writing
pages.text: An Age is not a chest to be filled, but a sentence to be spoken. Remember this law above all: $(c)a color must come before the thing it changes.$() $(br)$(br)Place a color immediately before its target. An $(thing)Age Effect$() marker must be paired with a non-instant status-effect page; their relative order does not matter.

pages.title: Grammar Leaks
pages.text: A loose omen is a leak in the binding. A color with nothing to stain adds a heavy penalty. An Age Effect marker with no status effect, or a status effect with no marker, also leaves the ink searching for meaning. Ink that must guess is ink that bites.

pages.title: Contradictions
pages.text: Do not command the same river to run both east and west. $(c)Fast Time$() beside $(c)Slow Time$(), rival shapes of land, rival weather, or both biome controllers will not stop the Age from forming. The last applicable choice wins, while every contradiction raises instability.

pages.title: Stable Basics
pages.text: For a gentle road, name the common pillars: $(li)land$(li)biomes$(li)time$(li)sun$(li)moon$(li)stars$(li)weather$() $(br)A plain truth is safer than a grand silence. A single well-named biome is often kinder than a dozen half-remembered wishes.

pages.title: The Wildcard
pages.text: The $(c)Random$() page is a dare written in ink. It invites the void to complete your thought. Sometimes it grants marvels: strange monuments, old bones, impossible surfaces. Sometimes it grants the sort of marvel that follows you home.
